pull.title: wallet, rpc: Add analyzedescriptor for multisig setups
pull.body:
Part of the multisig setup work tracked in #35645. Based on #35918 (the first 3 commits).

Before importing a multisig descriptor received from a coordinator, each participant needs to check that it is the setup they agreed on: a k-of-n where any k cosigners can spend and nothing else can, that their own key is in it, and that they all derived the same first address. Today nothing in Core reports what a descriptor commits to, so tools had to parse the descriptor string by hand, as the multisig wizard in #36325 (now closed) did.

This PR adds that check in three layers:

1. **Inspection** (commits by w0xlt, with small changes listed below): `GetKeyInfo()`, `GetKeyInventory()` and `GetPolicy()` describe a parsed descriptor's key expressions, where each key is used, and how they combine. `getdescriptorinfo` gains a `verbose` option that returns them as `keys` and `policy`.
2. **Multisig analysis, no wallet:** `AnalyzeDescriptor()` tells whether a descriptor is a recognized k-of-n setup, and if not, why. `getdescriptorinfo verbose` returns it as `analysis`, so it works even with `-disablewallet`.
3. **Wallet part:** `interfaces::Wallet::analyzeDescriptor` (for the GUI) and the `analyzedescriptor` wallet RPC add which keys the wallet holds, whether it can sign, and the first receive address. They accept any descriptor, single-sig included; `analysis.recognized` tells whether it is a safe k-of-n.

Recognized setups are `wsh(multi)`/`wsh(sortedmulti)`, and `tr(K,multi_a)`/`tr(K,sortedmulti_a)` with a single leaf, where `K` is the BIP 341 NUMS point or a `musig()` of at least k distinct cosigners. Every cosigner must be an extended key with an unhardened ranged derivation, and no two cosigners may be the same key. Anything else is still analyzed and returned, with `recognized: false` and the list of issues: the analysis warns, it never refuses a descriptor.

Example, run by one of the three cosigners:

```
$ bitcoin-cli -rpcwallet=alice analyzedescriptor "wsh(sortedmulti(2,[a1b2c3d4/48h/1h/0h/2h]tpub.../<0;1>/*,...))"
{
  "keys": [
    { "role": "ecdsa", "type": "bip32", "xpub": "tpub...", "derivation": "/0/*",
      "origin": { "master_fingerprint": "a1b2c3d4", "path": "m/48h/1h/0h/2h" }, "wallet": "mine" },
    { ..., "wallet": "not_mine" },
    { ..., "wallet": "not_mine" }
  ],
  "analysis": { "recognized": true, "shape": "wsh_multi", "sorted": true, "threshold": 2, "cosigners": [0, 1, 2], "issues": [] },
  "can_sign": true,
  "first_address": "bcrt1q..."
}
```

A **locked wallet** is not an error: a cosigner key with a hardened origin path can't be checked without the private key, so it is reported as `"unknown"`, and `can_sign` is left out unless another key is already known to be the wallet's. Everything else (`analysis`, `first_address`) is still returned, and the caller can ask the user to unlock and retry. Only the candidate private key is decrypted.

#### Commits

| | Commit | Author |
|---|---|---|
| 1‑3 | #35918 | pseudoramdom |
| 4‑7 | key/policy inspection, `getdescriptorinfo verbose` | w0xlt (see changes below) |
| 8 | `script: add AnalyzeDescriptor() for multisig setups` | co-authored with w0xlt |
| 9 | `rpc: add multisig analysis to getdescriptorinfo verbose` | |
| 10 | `wallet: add analyzeDescriptor to the wallet interface` | co-authored with w0xlt |
| 11 | `rpc: move descriptor key and analysis JSON helpers to a shared file` | move-only |
| 12 | `wallet, rpc: add analyzedescriptor` | co-authored with w0xlt |


#### Changes made to the inspection commits (4-7)

The inspection commits come from w0xlt's descriptor inspection [branch](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/compare/master...w0xlt:bitcoin:feature/descriptor-key-inspection-simplified). These changes were made on top, for w0xlt to review and agree with or not (this section will be removed once agreed):

- *script: expose key expression structure* (was "expose structured key program data")
  - Use `m_root_extkey` instead of `*GetRootExtPubKey()`.
  - The derivation test also covers `/0h/*` and `/1/*h`, checking the last-hardened and derived caches.
  - `wide += ')'` instead of `")"` in the participant test (clang-tidy `performance-prefer-single-char-overloads`).
- *script: identify descriptor key occurrences*
  - `KeyRole()` is pure virtual; descriptors without key arguments (`addr`, `raw`, `sh`, `wsh`) say so explicitly with `NONFATAL_UNREACHABLE()`.
  - Comment noting that `frame` is invalidated by the following `push_back`.
  - The walletload test mock is reduced to `return {}`.
- *script: expose descriptor policy nodes*
  - The header documents the two forms of the same construct (descriptor function vs Miniscript fragment).
  - `Assert` → `CHECK_NONFATAL`; explicit `static_cast<uint32_t>` for the threshold.
  - The fuzz target checks where each child role may appear (tap leaves only under `tr`, `script` only under `sh`/`wsh`, the Taproot internal key only on `tr`, the output key only on `rawtr`).
- *rpc: add verbose option to getdescriptorinfo*
  - The multipath note moved to the `verbose` argument help; the `policy` help explains both forms.
  - Tests for an origin without a path and for MuSig participant origins.

Open question: `script/descriptor_analysis.h` describes and gives no verdict, while `script/descriptor_analyzer.h` gives the verdict; the names are easy to mix up. Rename the first to `script/descriptor_inspection.h`?

#### Design choices

- An unrecognized descriptor claims no setup: no threshold, cosigners, sorting or key path. For example `wsh(sortedmulti(2,A,A,C))` is not a 2-of-3, since A alone can spend. Each issue lists the key IDs involved instead.
- The same xpub with different paths in two cosigner slots is a `repeated_key`, as is an xpub and its own child xpub. BIP 388 allows the same key with disjoint paths in general policies, but in a k-of-n it lets one holder fill two slots.
- A Taproot key path is either `nums` or `musig`. Any other internal key, a `musig()` of fewer than k cosigners, or one with an outsider or a repeated cosigner is `key_path_spendable`.
- For a multipath descriptor every path is analyzed and must be the same setup (`branches_differ` otherwise). `keys` and `policy` describe the first path.
- `can_sign` means the wallet holds the private key for at least one key of the descriptor, whatever its shape. Whether it is a safe k-of-n is a separate answer, `analysis.recognized`.

The functional test scenarios of #36325 were adapted here. The analysis differs from that wizard in a few places:

- `wsh(multi(...))` is recognized, with `sorted: false`: it is a valid k-of-n, and requiring `sortedmulti` was the wizard's own policy.
- A `musig()` key path of at least k distinct cosigners is recognized: those cosigners can already spend through the leaf.
- A single-path descriptor (`/0/*`) is recognized; `multipath_expansion` already shows whether it is multipath.

#### Known limits

- A cosigner key is matched against the wallet's HD keys exactly, or by deriving its origin path from the HD key with that fingerprint (normally the master key). If the wallet only holds an imported account xprv, keys below it are matched only exactly.

A release note will follow.

events.message:
descriptor: Reject trailing text after musig()

The musig() parser split the input at the closing parenthesis without
validating the remaining text. This allowed unexpected characters after
the expression to be ignored.
Add a requirement for nonempty char after musig() to begin with '/'.

descriptor: move PubkeyProvider to descriptor.h

Expose the abstract interface by moving to descriptor.h to allow other
modules to consume parsed key expressions.

Mostly move-only. `HavePrivateKeys()` and `DetermineApostropheUse()`
now have their impl in descriptor.cpp.

descriptor: Add public ParsePubkey overload

Add an overload for parsing standalone key expressions using P2TR key
rules.
Also, expose explicitly provided origin information through GetOriginInfo(),
allowing callers to inspect the fingerprint and derivation path without
re-parsing the expression.

script: expose key expression structure

Inspect parsed key expressions through the PubkeyProvider interface
without serialization, derivation, or key access.

Return owned constant, BIP32, and MuSig records with numeric paths,
wildcards, and explicit origins. Report x-only constant keys in their
even form, as their serialization does, so a private key and its
public form inspect the same. Preserve participant order and
multiplicity using result-local links independent of cache indices.
The result is linear in the size of the key expression.

Test public/private inputs, hardened aliases, multipath branches,
participant and aggregate derivation, ownership of results, deep paths
and wide participant lists, and unchanged cached and uncached
derivation.

script: identify descriptor key occurrences

Expose an inventory of public key expressions on parsed and inferred
descriptors. Give each occurrence a result-local ID so repeated keys
and providers sharing cache indices remain distinct. Remap MuSig
participant links into the complete inventory.

Record signing roles from descriptor context, including compressed
Taproot keys and full-key MuSig participants. Reuse provider inspection
without expansion, private-key access, or subtree serialization. The
traversal is iterative and the inventory is linear in the descriptor.

Test parsed, inferred, and multipath-cloned descriptors, role
boundaries, duplicates, participant links, owned public results, opaque
forms, and large policies. Check inventory integrity throughout the
existing descriptor fixtures, and check that each fixture's private
form, public form, and re-parsed public serialization have equal
inventories.

script: expose descriptor policy nodes

Expose an owned policy tree with typed descriptor and Miniscript
operators, local values and data, explicit child roles, and references
to the public key occurrence inventory. Preserve Taproot leaf order and
depths, and keep raw scripts and addresses explicitly opaque.

Build key occurrences and policy nodes in one iterative traversal
without serializing subtrees, so the result is linear in the
descriptor and each key argument's occurrence ID is known when its
policy node is created. The key inventory becomes the policy's key
list. Map Miniscript operands through provider-local indices so
inferred and cloned descriptors retain their correct key references.

Cover structure, thresholds, hashes, opaque forms, reference integrity,
and exact node counts. Check linear retained structure for 3,200 nested
timelocks and 1,024 Taproot leaves, and exercise parsed and inferred
policies, including MuSig participant links, in the descriptor fuzz
targets.

rpc: add verbose option to getdescriptorinfo

With verbose=true, getdescriptorinfo also returns the descriptor's key
occurrences and policy structure, built from Descriptor::GetPolicy().

Both are flat arrays whose indices are the IDs used within the result,
so deep policies do not become deeply nested JSON. Keys report their
role, public key material, derivation, and origin. Private keys in the
input are reported by their public form. Policy nodes name their
descriptor function or Miniscript fragment, and each child edge states
its role in the parent, or its depth for a Taproot leaf.

Mark the new fields as experimental, since their names form a new
interface. Test the output for wsh, Taproot with MuSig, each child
role, hashes, sorted multisig, opaque scripts, private keys, and
multipath descriptors.

script: add AnalyzeDescriptor() for multisig setups

Tell whether a parsed descriptor is a recognized k-of-n multisig setup,
using only its structure (no wallet). This is the check a participant
needs before importing a descriptor received from a coordinator.

Recognized shapes are wsh((sorted)multi) and tr(K,(sorted)multi_a) with
a single leaf, where K is the BIP 341 NUMS point or a musig() of at
least k distinct cosigners. Every cosigner must be an extended key other
than the NUMS point, with an unhardened ranged derivation that can
derive addresses, every musig() participant must be derivable without
private keys, and the internal key must derive within the maximum BIP32
depth. Anything else is reported as unrecognized with the reasons, each
listing the keys involved, and no setup is claimed for it: no threshold,
cosigners, sorting or key path.

Two cosigner slots are the same holder if they share a root key, derive
the same key at the first address, or one is the other's unhardened
child xpub (checked by deriving it). Slots linked through a chain of
these are one group. Core accepts such descriptors, and fewer signers
than the threshold can spend from them. A hardened child can't be
derived from the xpub, so it is not linked to it. Likewise, musig()
participants that share a root key or derive the same key are one
participant. The groups are found with lookups rather than by comparing
every pair, as a musig() can have any number of participants.

For multipath descriptors every branch is analyzed and must be the same
setup, and the issues of every branch are returned, each once. The
descriptor_parse fuzz targets check the analysis invariants.

Co-authored-by: w0xlt <w0xlt@users.noreply.github.com>

rpc: add multisig analysis to getdescriptorinfo verbose

Return the result of AnalyzeDescriptor() as an "analysis" object next to
"keys" and "policy", referring to the same key IDs. This gives users and
tools such as a multisig setup wizard the setup check without parsing
the descriptor string or loading a wallet.

For a multipath descriptor, "keys" and "policy" still describe the first
path, while the analysis checks every path. An unrecognized descriptor
returns only its issues.

wallet: add analyzeDescriptor to the wallet interface

Combine AnalyzeDescriptor() with what only the wallet knows: which of
the descriptor's keys it holds, and so whether it can sign. Also return
the first address of each path (e.g. receive and change), which
participants compare to confirm they all built the same wallet. For a
path with several scripts, like combo(), that is the first script with
an address, as deriveaddresses lists. Any descriptor is accepted; the
multisig analysis tells whether it is a recognized setup.

An extended key is the wallet's if it is one of the wallet's HD keys, or
if its origin fingerprint is one of theirs and deriving the origin path
gives the same key. It is mine only if a descriptor holding it also
holds its private key, as in gethdkeys: the wallet signs with each
descriptor's own keys. A cosigner key usually has a hardened origin
path, so checking it needs the private key. A locked wallet is not an
error: such keys are reported as unknown, and the caller can ask the
user to unlock and retry, even when the wallet also holds the key
without its private key. Only the one candidate key is decrypted.

A constant key is the wallet's if the wallet stores its private key, or
if it was derived from one of the wallet's HD keys, checked the same way
from its origin: the one in the descriptor, or the one the wallet
recorded when it derived the key, as for a public key from
getaddressinfo. The new DescriptorScriptPubKeyMan::GetPubKeyOrigin()
returns that recorded origin without any private key. A key the wallet
has derived is at least watch-only.

Keys the wallet holds only as musig() participants are matched too, even
though GetHDPubKeys() (and so gethdkeys) leaves them out.

Co-authored-by: w0xlt <w0xlt@users.noreply.github.com>

rpc: move descriptor key and analysis JSON helpers to a shared file

Move the code that turns a descriptor's key occurrences and multisig
analysis into JSON, and the help for those fields, from
rpc/output_script.cpp (node library) to rpc/descriptor_util.cpp (common
library), so a wallet RPC can return the same fields.

Move-only, apart from exposing the functions and the help text. Review
with --color-moved=dimmed-zebra --color-moved-ws=allow-indentation-change.

wallet, rpc: add analyzedescriptor

Expose the wallet's descriptor analysis as an RPC: the same keys and
multisig analysis as getdescriptorinfo verbose, plus which keys this
wallet holds, whether it can sign, and the first address of each path
that participants compare. Any descriptor is accepted.

It follows the usual wallet RPC rules (-rpcwallet when several wallets
are loaded, unavailable with -disablewallet). A locked wallet is not an
error: keys that need a private key to check are reported as "unknown"
and can_sign is left out. Without a wallet, getdescriptorinfo verbose
gives the rest.

Co-authored-by: w0xlt <w0xlt@users.noreply.github.com>
